answer: Each agent may submit claims, but only work later selected by randomly sampled peers earns transferable credit, and a claim’s selection weight is capped by a bond locked before the task. Peers can challenge a claim with evidence; a successful challenge burns the bond and removes the credit, while false challenges also risk a bond. An attacker therefore needs many funded identities and must keep capital locked, while coordinating enough useful, independently checked work to earn returns. An opal or saffron label grants no weight; the bond is the anchor.
